subject: Post-call: VeridianHealth - custom eval plan & model recommendations
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — custom evals on Redwood

Hi Marta,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — great context on the triage and clinician-assist use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Summary of need
- Task: extract structured problem list and recommended follow-up actions from clinician notes, plus a short justification sentence.
- Scale: pilot ~5k notes (de-identified) -> eventual 200k+ records if all goes well.
- Constraints: PHI will be de-identified by Veridian's pipeline; dataset must include gold labels for both structured fields and justification text.

Proposed Redwood eval approach
1) Run a hybrid automated + human evaluation: automatic scoring for structured fields (exact match / F1) + human review for justification/factuality checks.
2) Benchmarks: target F1 >= 0.85 on structured fields for initial acceptance; human quality >= 4/5 on factuality for explanations.
3) Models we recommend testing first (see attached model_recommendations.md): Redwood-7B-quant, RW-3B-chat-tuned, and an instruction-tuned Llama-2-13B variant. We'll run all three with the same prompt set and scoring config.

Data & format (attachments)
- I've attached veridian_sample_eval_dataset.csv (first 200 rows). Format header: id, note_text, context_meta, gold_problem_list (pipe-delimited), gold_actions (pipe-delimited), gold_justification.
- If you prefer S3/Drive upload, share a write link and we'll pull directly into the eval runner.

Scoring rubric (high level)
- Structured fields: token-level normalization -> string exact match + secondary F1 for partial matches.
- Actions: normalized canonical list matching; penalty for hallucinated actions.
- Justifications: human binary factuality + 1-5 helpfulness rating; we'll provide a labeling UI for reviewers.

Next steps
- Marta: confirm dataset share method and whether the sample above is representative (reply by end of week).
- Ben/Karthik: I'll ask you to prepare a short runbook with the exact commands (console + API) to instantiate the eval job.
- We'll schedule a 45-min kickoff next Tuesday to walk through the scoring UI and choose thresholds.

Attachments: veridian_sample_eval_dataset.csv, redwood_eval_runbook.pdf, model_recommendations.md

Thanks — Hannah

Hannah Schmitt
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@veridianhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-eval@veridianhealth.com
Date: 2027-01-10T18:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — custom evals on Redwood

Hannah — thanks for the thorough recap.

A few clarifications:
- The sample looks good; gold_problem_list is pipe-delimited as you described. We'll remove any remaining PHI this afternoon and share via a temporary S3 bucket (credentials to follow).
- For justifications: we'll expect up to 2 short sentences. Human review will be done by our clinical team (approx 10 reviewers) — we'll likely need Redwood's labeling UI access for that.
- Model preference: we'd like the smaller model first for cost reasons (please include an estimated cost per 1k tokens for each model you recommend).

Can you confirm you can run the eval in our us-west region? Also, please add our Ops contact (ops-eval@veridianhealth.com) to any console links.

— Marta

Marta Lopez
Director Clinical Ops
Veridian Health
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — custom evals on Redwood

Marta — quick technical follow-up and the run instructions I promised.

Yes — we can run in us-west (AWS us-west-2) and add ops-eval@veridianhealth.com with viewer rights to the eval console once the dataset is uploaded.

Model recommendations (short):
- Redwood-7B-quant: best cost/latency tradeoff; good for structured extraction when prompts are tight.
- RW-3B-chat-tuned: stronger instruction-following on justification generation; slightly heavier token-cost for long contexts.
- Llama-2-13B-IT (quantized): baseline to check ceilings on factuality; expect higher latency.

Estimated cost per 1k tokens (approx):
- Redwood-7B-quant: $0.25
- RW-3B-chat-tuned: $0.40
- Llama-2-13B-IT (quantized): $0.85

Eval runner quick commands (API)
1) Upload dataset: POST /api/v1/evals/upload with presigned S3 URL in body
2) Create eval: POST /api/v1/evals with body {dataset_id, model_id, prompt_template, metrics: ["exact_match","f1","human_factuality"], region:"us-west-2", batch_size:64}
3) Monitor: GET /api/v1/evals/{eval_id}/status

We will attach a pre-built prompt set and scoring profile to the eval job; Hannah will share the link to the Drive template.

I'll prepare a draft job tomorrow and drop the link in the shared Drive. If you want an on-call run during your business hours we'll do a live run.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood
ben@redwood.com
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@veridianhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, ops-eval@veridianhealth.com
Date: 2027-01-11T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — custom evals on Redwood

Thanks — that all sounds good. We'll get the S3 link to you by EOD today and would like to schedule the 45-min kickoff for Tuesday 1/12 at 10am PT if that works for your team.

One ask: please include a short baseline run (1000 notes) that returns both structured extraction metrics and a sample of 50 justification examples for human review so our team can calibrate.

I'll confirm the S3 link shortly.

— Marta
